reviewedRevision: 5f03a9f plus the rework in this commit
process: Lean final review at the user's request: the known 3-course shortfall went straight to a retrofit, followed by one independent review round. Its BLOCKING blind-play finding and two MEDIUM findings were fixed and verified by re-running the reviewer's own blind, pilot, floor-scan, determinism and fuzz scripts, one clean-worktree run and the browser check, without a second review round.
independentProbes: On the final files the reviewer's reaction-limited climber (public state, 0.35 s delay, no prediction) cleared mastery routes 15-20 in 104 of 120 runs (86.7%), losing about 1.1 lives per cleared route, while at 0.25 s it cleared 399 of 400 runs over all 20 routes. Seventeen blind families (idle, mash, random and timed hold, alternate and hook patterns, including the former hold Right+Up and tap exploit at 1.0-1.4 s) won 1.0% overall with the worst family at 6.9%; route 9 alone won 0 of 510. A fine scan of 11,914 standing hooks found no floor penetration beyond 0.002 px. Sixty scripts matched to 0.000 px across 30, 60 and 120 Hz, the hostile-input fuzz was clean, and broken progress stores were safe. In the review round the stall guard never froze play unfairly, rescue never double-spent a life, and anchor taps selected only eligible anchors.

findings.observation: Only 3 courses built from inline plans, with no select or continue. There are now 20 data-driven routes (teaching 1-7, combination 8-14, mastery 15-20) with rope-cutting rocks, moving rails, long gaps and narrow cairns, accurate EN/ZH tips, a route select and env.progress continue; a stall guard ends a wedge hang, rescue-pause taps are queued, anchors can be tapped, and the 1,774-line file is split into eight modules.

Review finding: holding Right and Up while tapping Space every 1.3 s cleared 45.8% of routes 3-20. A hook from a cairn now needs the climber standing still (a visible bilingual notice explains a refusal), a mid-air hook is refused after falling below the lowest cairn top, and middle and exit cairns narrow by tier.

Review finding: mastery cost the climber almost no lives and rocks acted as free auto-releases. Mastery routes now use faster, wider rails (route 16 needs two swings, route 18 a lower rail), and a rock cutting a hanging rope costs a life, with corrected tips on routes 2, 6 and 9.

Review finding: hooking while standing under a moving anchor could sink the climber 7 px into the cairn and drop them through it. A penetration resolver now pushes the climber out along the face normal and books the energy change, with tests on routes 4, 15, 16, 18 and 19.

openNotes: Mastery clears sit just above the target (86.7% at 0.35 s); routes 16 and 19 are the hardest.
Hooking requires standing still, so touch players release the walk button before tapping Hook.
Routes have at most three cairns; the canvas leaves no room for longer chains.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start and the touch buttons, synthetic in-page keys; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: English: Start opened route 1 of 20 (Copper Arch) with 5 lives and the winch meter; standing still, Space hooked the marked anchor and the rope and landing guide appeared.
Holding Left and pressing Space showed 'Stand still to hook: let go of Left and Right, then press Space.'

English 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): nine touch buttons (Walk left, Walk right, Target, Hook / release, Reel in, Pay out, Rescue −1 life, Next route) with the route opening unobscured.
Not covered in the browser: a route win and a loss; the reviewer's climber and the quality tests cover them.
